# Node.js Project Setup Reference

This skill contains the complete, canonical setup steps for every Node.js backend project taught in this course. When writing notes or helping with setup, always follow these conventions exactly.

---

## Complete Project Folder Structure

Every project must follow this layout. The entry point is `src/server.js`, not `app.js`.

```
project-name/
  src/
    server.js            <- starts the Express server, imports routes, middleware
    controllers/
      userController.js  <- logic for handling user routes
      productController.js
    middlewares/
      logger.js          <- custom logging middleware
      errorHandler.js    <- global error handling middleware
      auth.js            <- JWT verification middleware
    routes/
      userRoutes.js      <- Express Router, maps URLs to controllers
      productRoutes.js
    db/
      prisma.js          <- creates and exports the Prisma client
    generated/
      prisma/            <- auto-generated by Prisma, never edit manually
  prisma/
    schema.prisma        <- define your database models here
    migrations/          <- auto-created when you run prisma migrate
    prisma.config.js     <- Prisma configuration (renamed from .ts)
  .env                   <- all secret/environment config, never commit this
  .gitignore             <- tell Git what to ignore
  docker-compose.yaml    <- defines the PostgreSQL container
  package.json
  package-lock.json
```

---

## Step 1: Initialize the Project

```bash
# Create the folder and enter it
mkdir my-project
cd my-project

# Initialize Node.js project with defaults
npm init -y
```

---

## Step 2: Install Packages

Run these two commands every time you start a new Node.js backend project.

```bash
# Production packages
npm i express dotenv pg @prisma/client @prisma/adapter-pg

# Development packages (only needed during development)
npm i prisma --save-dev
npm i -D nodemon
```

Package explanations:

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| express | Web framework for building APIs |
| dotenv | Loads .env file into process.env |
| pg | PostgreSQL driver (lets Node.js talk to Postgres) |
| @prisma/client | The auto-generated Prisma query client |
| @prisma/adapter-pg | Connects Prisma to PostgreSQL using pg driver |
| prisma | CLI tool for migrations and schema management |
| nodemon | Auto-restarts the server when you save a file |

---

## Step 3: Configure package.json

After `npm init -y`, open `package.json` and update it to look like this:

```json
{
  "name": "my-project",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "src/server.js",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "node src/server.js",
    "dev": "nodemon src/server.js"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@prisma/adapter-pg": "...",
    "@prisma/client": "...",
    "dotenv": "...",
    "express": "...",
    "pg": "..."
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "nodemon": "...",
    "prisma": "..."
  }
}
```

Key points:
- `"type": "module"` enables ES module syntax (`import`/`export`)
- `"start"` runs the production server
- `"dev"` runs nodemon which restarts automatically on file save

---

## Step 4: Create the .env File

Create `.env` in the project root (same level as `package.json`):

```
PORT=8888
POSTGRES_USER=userdipak
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=user_password
POSTGRES_DB=student_record
POSTGRES_HOST=localhost
POSTGRES_PORT=5555

# DATABASE_URL format: postgresql://user:password@host:port/databaseName?schema=public
DATABASE_URL="postgresql://userdipak:user_password@localhost:5555/student_record?schema=public"
```

Change `userdipak`, `user_password`, and `student_record` to match your actual values.

---

## Step 5: Create the .gitignore File

Create `.gitignore` in the project root:

```
# Dependencies
node_modules/

# Environment variables (NEVER commit this)
.env

# Build output
dist/

# Prisma generated files (optional, regenerated with prisma generate)
# src/generated/
```

---

## Step 6: Create docker-compose.yaml

Create `docker-compose.yaml` in the project root. This defines the PostgreSQL database container.

```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16
    restart: always
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
    ports:
      - "${POSTGRES_PORT}:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  pgdata:
```

The `${VARIABLE}` syntax reads values from your `.env` file automatically.

### Podman Commands

This course uses Podman instead of Docker (they use the same compose file format):

```bash
# Start the database container with logs visible
podman compose up

# Start the database container in background (silent)
podman compose up -d

# Stop the containers
podman compose down
```

Start the database container before running your Node.js server.

---

## Step 7: Initialize Prisma

```bash
npx prisma init
```

This creates:
- `prisma/schema.prisma` - your database schema file
- `prisma/prisma.config.ts` - rename this to `prisma.config.js`

```bash
# Rename the config file
mv prisma/prisma.config.ts prisma/prisma.config.js
```

---

## Step 8: Configure schema.prisma

Open `prisma/schema.prisma` and update it to exactly this (for JavaScript projects):

```prisma
generator client {
  provider     = "prisma-client-js"
  output       = "../src/generated/prisma"
  moduleFormat = "esm"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
}
```

Explanation of each line:
- `provider = "prisma-client-js"` tells Prisma to generate a JavaScript client
- `output = "../src/generated/prisma"` puts the generated client inside `src/generated/prisma/`
- `moduleFormat = "esm"` generates ES module format (matching `"type": "module"` in package.json)
- `provider = "postgresql"` tells Prisma the database is PostgreSQL
- No `url` is needed in datasource because Prisma reads `DATABASE_URL` from `.env` automatically

---

## Step 9: Create src/db/prisma.js

Create the folder first: `mkdir -p src/db`

Then create `src/db/prisma.js`:

```javascript
import 'dotenv/config';

// Import PrismaClient from the generated output folder
// This matches the output path in schema.prisma: "../src/generated/prisma"
import { PrismaClient } from '../generated/prisma/client.js';

// Import the PostgreSQL adapter that connects Prisma to the pg driver
import { PrismaPg } from '@prisma/adapter-pg';

// Create the adapter using the DATABASE_URL from .env
const adapter = new PrismaPg({
  connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL,
});

// Create the Prisma client and pass the adapter
const prisma = new PrismaClient({ adapter });

// Export it so other files can use it
export default prisma;
```

Note: if you want to use `import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'` instead, remove the `output` line from `schema.prisma` and run `npx prisma generate` again.

---

## Step 10: Add Models to schema.prisma

Example model for a User table:

```prisma
model User {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  name      String
  email     String   @unique
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
}
```

---

## Step 11: Run Migrations

```bash
# Create and run migration (replace "create_users_table" with your description)
npx prisma migrate dev --name create_users_table
```

Other useful Prisma commands:

```bash
# Open the visual database browser
npx prisma studio

# Reset database (drops all data and re-runs migrations from scratch)
npx prisma migrate reset

# Regenerate the Prisma client after schema changes
npx prisma generate
```

---

## Step 12: Create src/server.js

```javascript
import 'dotenv/config';           // load .env first
import express from 'express';

const app = express();

// Parse JSON request bodies
app.use(express.json());

const PORT = process.env.PORT || 8888;

// Health check route
app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ message: 'Server is running' });
});

// Start the server
app.listen(PORT, () => {
  console.log(`Server running at http://localhost:${PORT}`);
});
```

---

## Quick Start Checklist

Use this checklist every time you start a new project:

- [ ] `mkdir project-name && cd project-name`
- [ ] `npm init -y`
- [ ] Add `"type": "module"` and scripts to `package.json`
- [ ] `npm i express dotenv pg @prisma/client @prisma/adapter-pg`
- [ ] `npm i prisma --save-dev && npm i -D nodemon`
- [ ] Create `.env` with PORT, POSTGRES vars, and DATABASE_URL
- [ ] Create `.gitignore` with node_modules/ and .env
- [ ] Create `docker-compose.yaml`
- [ ] `podman compose up -d` to start the database
- [ ] `npx prisma init`
- [ ] Rename `prisma.config.ts` to `prisma.config.js`
- [ ] Update `prisma/schema.prisma` with the correct generator and datasource
- [ ] Create `src/db/prisma.js`
- [ ] Add your models to `schema.prisma`
- [ ] `npx prisma migrate dev --name init`
- [ ] Create `src/server.js` and start with `npm run dev`
